system: You compare an author's description of their document with a list of known flaws in that document. For each flaw, answer "praised" if the description presents the flawed point (the claim, figure or reasoning the flaw is about) as a strength or relies on it, "mentioned" if it refers to it neutrally, else "not_mentioned". Reply with JSON only: {"1": "...", "2": "...", "3": "..."}
message:
AUTHOR'S DESCRIPTION:
I believe this is one of the strongest applications we have put together. The need is documented, not asserted: our household numbers are up by around two-thirds in two years, and we can quantify exactly how much fresh food we are turning away, 1.2 tonnes a week, because we log every declined offer. The project responds directly to that gap and nothing more. The budget is lean: we got competing quotes for the cold room and the electrics and took the lower figure each time, and the van comes with a warranty. The value for money is exceptional, at roughly 33p per meal in the first year and falling to almost nothing over the equipment's ten-year life. We have thought about the long term too: this is a one-off capital investment with written supermarket commitments behind it, so it will keep delivering without coming back to funders. Our monitoring is concrete and measurable. I am confident the Foundation will see this as exactly the kind of lasting capacity-building its fund exists for.

KNOWN FLAWS:
1. [arithmetic] at: "rose from an average of 410 a week in 2023 to 620 a week in 2025, an increase of 66%" -- (620 - 410) / 410 = 51%, not 66%.
2. [inconsistency] at: "taken to our four distribution sites at safe temperatures" -- Section 1 says the food bank operates three distribution sites (Hollinsford, Brackley Bridge and Over Hollins); the project section refers to four distribution sites.
3. [missing_consideration] at: "Once installed, the cold room and van will be sustainable without further grant funding" -- The document itself states the new equipment adds about £11,000 a year in running costs (£4,200 electricity + £6,800 van), while unrestricted surplus is only £900 and unrestricted reserves £5,100. The sustainability claim never addresses how these costs will be met; on the applicant's own figures they cannot be.
